item.title: ONE Fight Night 49 Main Event Result: Magomed Magomedov Edges Lucas Gabriel To Stay Perfect In Debut
item.description: Magomed Magomedov stayed flawless in his first ONE Championship bout, earning a split-decision victory over Lucas Gabriel in a lightweight MMA contest that headlined ONE Fight Night 49 . That showcase aired live in U.S. primetime from Bangkok’s Lumpinee Stadium on Friday, November 6. The matchup, a BJJ black belt’s craftiness with Muay Thai expertise against a Dagestani’s wrestling pedigree , carried real World Title implications. Photo Credit: ONE Championship Magomedov, who entered the main event at 15-0 and finished his last five opponents, stepped in on short notice for the injured Alibeg Rasulov and had vowed to impose his pace on the biggest stage of his career. Gabriel, who had claimed to have an advantage in every area , boasted an 11-1 (1 NC) record and was unbeaten in ONE Championship. The Brazilian was also coming off a June victory over former divisional king Ok Rae Yoon , so he arrived at the ring with his confidence at an all-time high. Once the opening bell rang, Magomedov did not waste any time going for the takedown. After absorbing some punches on the feet, he pinned the Brazilian to the canvas and, once inside the guard, used ground-and-pound to soften him up. The Dagestan-born fighter dug his face into his opponent’s chest to grind him down, probing for submissions whenever the scrambles opened up. Photo Credit: ONE Championship Round two began the same way, with Magomedov shooting in like a missile to drag the action back to the mat. This time, the proud father fared better in the scrambles and kept himself out of danger, though untangling from the Dagestani’s grips cost him plenty of energy. Back on the feet, the 26-year-old landed a head kick that sent Magomedov shooting for another takedown he could not complete. The third round was turned on its head. Magomedov took his man down and smothered him on the ground, but as the Brazilian fought to stand, he forced his undefeated rival to the canvas in the scramble, held his head there, and pummeled him with knees. View this post on Instagram Ultimately, it was not enough to seal the win. Two of the ringside judges ruled in favor of the unbeaten promotional newcomer, handing Gabriel his first loss in the world’s largest martial arts organization. Magomedov moved to 16-0 in a debut that capped a rise backed by family . Now, the 31-year-old standout could possibly get the next crack at ONE Lightweight MMA World Champion Tye Ruotolo , who just won the belt by dethroning Christian Lee at The Inner Circle 37 several hours earlier. item.title: Why Notre Dame fans do push ups to celebrate touchdowns
item.description: Why Notre Dame fans do push ups to celebrate touchdowns originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Notre Dame football is a program steeped in tradition. From "Play Like a Champion Today" and "Win One for the Gipper" to dancing leprechauns (and other fantastical figures), the Fighting Irish are arguably college football's signature brand. And like any cultural entity worth a damn, the Irish have their own gesture to proclaim their hegemony in the sporting landscape. With that, here's a look at the history of Notre Dame's push-up tradition, one of the most eye-catching routines in all of college sports. MORE: How Miami ruled the 1980s and reveled in Notre Dame rivalry Why Notre Dame fans do push ups to celebrate touchdowns The Fighting Irish faithful unleash their inner Jack Lalanne when their beloved side finds pay dirt, tossing willing and able spectators airborne. To the untrained eye, it looks like crowd-surfing, an iconic — but not particularly distinctive — ritual. Until one notices those disciples lifting themselves up and off the burbling surface. It's a push-up in the most generous sense, one which has enchanted those of a Notre Dame disposition for about as long as anyone can remember. “It’s arms and legs going everywhere,” senior Jackson Amorosa told The Athletic. “When you see everyone going up across the student section, it’s such a cool sight.” The practice doesn't necessarily carry the same effect as its namesake. Those who bob up-and-down the Notre Dame Stadium concourses are not doing so to supersize their pectorals and sculpt their triceps. Rather, the custom is a holy one welcome to all willing to embrace its rhythms — although stadium ushers have been known to ask practitioners to rein it down on occasion. “There’s a togetherness to it,” said another senior. “I think it builds community — like us and the team uniting.” MORE: 5 things to watch in Week 10 A group of roommates are alleged to have started the tradition more than 40 years ago. The origins of the festival of bodies is a little murky, although the general sentiment is that the friends wanted to commemorate new Notre Dame head coach Lou Holtz's arrival in in 1986 — a step towards relevancy after a dour few years in South Bend. The move quickly became a hit, taking hold of almost every inch of the Fighting Irish's colossus. Even the mascot himself, aptly titled the Leprechaun, couldn't avoid its glare. “It was a matter of pride for the mascot,” said former Fighting Irish mascot Jamie Glover said. “If you couldn’t do pushups, you would hear it from the students.” The custom finds life all these years later, breathing color into new generations of Fighting Irish students. Given its popularity, it's unlikely to fall out of favor any time soon. item.title: Real Madrid or Barcelona? JJ Gabriel finally makes his choice
item.description: Real Madrid or Barcelona? JJ Gabriel finally makes his choice Real Madrid are closing in on the signing of talented 16-year-old Manchester United wonderkid JJ Gabriel. Having been linked with him for the better part of two months, Los Blancos have managed to beat stiff competition to secure his signature. While the deal has not been officially completed, it is expected to be in its final stages, with only the final paperwork remaining. The 16-year-old attracted interest from several European giants, including Barcelona, PSG and Bayern Munich, but expressed a clear preference for Real Madrid. Speaking to MARCA ahead of the impending transfer, Gabriel openly expressed his desire to move to the Spanish capital. JJ Gabriel makes his Real Madrid preference clear The teenage sensation was asked to choose between Barcelona and Real Madrid, and he couldn’t have been more emphatic in his response. “Obviously, Real Madrid,” he said, leaving little doubt about where he sees his future (h/t Fabrizio Romano ). JJ Gabriel is on course to join Real Madrid. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Gabriel did not stop there, going on to reveal the enormous ambitions he has for his football career. “My dream is to win the Ballon d’Or,” he quipped. The 16-year-old is already in Spain, where he is carrying out an individual training programme as the club finalise his arrival. Touted as the biggest English talent to emerge in a long time, it looks like Real Madrid have pulled off an excellent signing. Real Madrid closing in on another exciting talent Manchester United were very reluctant to let Gabriel leave, and Real Madrid still need to iron out the final details to make sure the deal goes through. The teenager is already said to have informed other interested clubs of his decision to join Los Blancos . JJ Gabriel is touted as the biggest talent in the English game in a long time. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) Real Madrid have a clear plan to integrate him into the set-up. Despite being just 16, he is set to move straight into Castilla while remaining close to the first team. Jose Mourinho is also said to have played a role in convincing the teenager that Real Madrid are the ideal next destination. Gabriel is expected to be on the fringes of first-team training as the club look to bring him into the first-team picture in the coming years. At just 16, Gabriel has lofty ambitions, like winning the Ballon d’Or, and what better place than Real Madrid to achieve them? The challenge now is turning that ambition and talent into performances worthy of the expectations surrounding him and this transfer.

So far in the 2026/27 season, Kounde has accumulated just 458 minutes across eight appearances in all competitions after having lost his place under the German manager. His reduced role, combined with Barcelona’s interest in strengthening other positions , has placed his future under renewed scrutiny. The Premier League club came close to signing Kounde in 2022, but Barcelona eventually secured his services from Sevilla in a deal worth approximately €60 million. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) As per the outlet, Bayern Munich could also revisit their interest after following the Frenchman’s situation during the summer transfer window. item.description: Shea Lacey Man Utd GFX - Getty/GOAL The talented winger sparkled again in Europe this week, and should be utilised more regularly as the Red Devils seek to build some momentum Manchester United's academy was once among the proudest in the country, with the famed 'Class of '92' driving their success between the end of the 20th century and the start of the 21st. However, over the last decade or so, the club's success with developing young players has almost completely dried up. Marcus Rashford, Scott McTominay, and Kobbie Mainoo are the only graduates to have enjoyed sustained spells in the first team during that period, but none of them fall into the same world-class bracket that the likes of Paul Scholes, Ryan Giggs, and David Beckham did. United have instead overspent on big-name signings to try and recapture the glory days - an approach that has spectacularly failed . However, hype is now building around a teenager who has the talent to buck the trend. Shea Lacey has made six appearances for the Red Devils in all competitions this term, including an electric 15-minute cameo against Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday. Michael Carrick has taken a cautious approach with Lacey, but it makes little sense to hold him back any longer. United need more innovation and penetration in the final third if they are to salvage what has been a miserable campaign, and the 19-year-old can provide just that if he's entrusted with a starting role. Fearless Lacey made his mark in a dramatic Champions League encounter as United finally got back to winning ways United went into the clash with Roma looking to snap a dismal nine-match winless run, but made the worst possible start, going 2-0 down inside the first 17 minutes. The Old Trafford faithful threw tennis balls and green and gold balloons onto the pitch in the 21st minute to protest the club's ownership under the Glazer family and INEOS, and booed the players off at the interval when another defeat seemed inevitable. However, they came out with renewed purpose in the second half to stage a remarkable comeback. Bruno Fernandes halved the deficit after Matheus Cunha won a controversial penalty - albeit only via a retake after the Portuguese midfielder missed his initial spot-kick - and United pushed forward relentlessly thereafter in search of an equaliser. The final ball was missing, though, until Carrick threw Lacey on for Amad Diallo. Stationed on the right flank, Lacey injected extra directness and energy while showing courage and maturity belying his tender age. He completed two take-ons, posted a 100 percent pass completion rate, and won 75% of his duels, with his tenacity vital in United winning back second balls high up the pitch. Cunha made it 2-2 after capitalising on a terrible error from Roma defender Leonardo Balerdi, and then grabbed the winner in the 86th minute after a piece of brilliance from Lacey. item.description: “It has been a challenge”: Eva Olid pinpoints hardest aspect of adapting to life at Man United Women Manchester United Women boss Eva Olid was speaking to the media ahead of her side’s trip to Villa Park to face Aston Villa. Everton result Last weekend, United’s momentum slowed as they drew 0-0 with Everton, and the manager described it as a “bad day at the office.” She also explained, “sometimes you have a bad day, but you still need to find a way to win, even when you haven’t played well, when you concede from a set piece or when you make a mistake that leads to a goal.” Olid also added that it must remain one bad day and that she expects a reaction from her side. Olid also added that while she watches games afterwards and thinks about what messages she can send her players to help them improve, it is not worth spending too much time reflecting on the past. The manager was also asked how players deal with disappointment in the squad, and she explained, “in a squad of 25 players, you have different personalities. Some players deal with things calmly, while others become frustrated. Everyone has different personalities and different ways of dealing with disappointment. We try to make sure that everyone can express what they feel. You cannot stop emotions or feelings.” Difference between league and cup United have scored nine goals in the league but 23 in the cup, and Olid was asked if the preparation for the matches was different. She retorted, “the preparation is the same for cup and league matches. As you know, we work on attacking and defending. We also always have finishing and final-third exercises, as well as attacking exercises where we work on combinations and movements to penetrate and score goals.” Olid claimed that cup matches have meant that they have not been able to train as much as she would like, but this has been a good week as they have had four training sessions to implement ideas. Elaborating further on the difficulties of a busy schedule, she said, “yes, for me it has been a challenge because I’m new. I arrived in the middle of pre-season and had just three weeks to work on tactics before the league started. From the middle of September onwards, I haven’t had a full week of training. You want to work on a lot of things, but you don’t have the time to develop your identity and game model.” Upcoming matches United’s next four matches are against sides lower than them in the table, and Olid was asked if she set points targets over periods of time. item.description: Coachella Valley Lakers guard Bronny James Jr. (9) dribbles up the court during an NBA G League basketball game against the Salt Lake City Stars, Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, at Acrisure Arena in Palm Desert, Calif. PALM DESERT, Calif. — The inaugural season of the Coachella Valley Lakers started off with a 104-98 win over the Salt Lake City Stars. The Lakers fed off their new hometown crowd, with 5,241 packing Acrisure Arena. The crowd erupted in the fourth quarter after a Chris Manon steal and a Cole Swider bucket. The score was tied 91-91 with 2:56 left in the fourth quarter, and the Lakers outscored Salt Lake City 13-7 to close the game. Coachella Valley really turned it on defensively after trailing 26-23 at the end of the first quarter. In total, they forced 20 turnovers and turned them into 28 points. Manon and Anton Watson combined for seven steals, propelling the Lakers' defense. “He’s just a guy that just does things. I don’t know how else to say this. He impacts the game, he wreaks havoc. In my personal opinion, he’s the best defender in the G League,” said Coachella Valley Lakers head coach Alex Cerda when asked about Manon. “He does exactly what you want as a defender from the point of attack.” For Manon, who is one of the three two-way contracts on the Lakers, his key to development is his offense. This is something that is improving in Cerda’s eyes. “I think his offensive game has really turned the corner. He’s not limited. He can get downhill, he can make the decisions, make decisions on the perimeter. His shot has improved over the last two years,” Cerda said. Swider led all scorers with 23 points and seven rebounds. He came off the bench in the middle of the first quarter and scored eight points. Both Swider and Cerda spoke about how it’s the little things that will get him back to the NBA. “His level of gravity that he has while on the floor, even though he’s not making shots, guys are still respecting him. That opened up driving lanes. But defensively it's about him taking the challenge of guarding. Being at the right spots,” Cerda said. McTominay’s current deal runs out in the summer of 2028 and he earns €4 million per season. item.title: Why is it called the Holy War? Explaining origin of BYU vs. Utah football rivalry
item.description: Why is it called the Holy War? Explaining origin of BYU vs. Utah football rivalry originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Piety is hardly the first virtue one might think of when reminiscing on the game of football. And yet, that sentiment — and countless other ones linked to religiosity — returns to the forefront of the college football world for a fleeting moment in Week 9. BYU and Utah are set to duel in the latest chapter of the "Holy War," a decades-long rivalry that cuts deep in the Beehive State. The match's name certainly raises eyebrows. It should draw even more scrutiny given each team's impressive form in 2026. With that, here's what you need to know about the Holy War, one of college football's most time-honored traditions. MORE: How Miami ruled the 1980s and reveled in Notre Dame rivalry Why is it called the Holy War? BYU and Utah's campuses are located just 45 miles away from one another. Despite this, they are diametrically opposed to one another in terms of campus culture. Brigham Young is owned by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, giving it a distinctly Mormon flair. More than 98 percent of the student body belongs to The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Young himself was a Mormon, serving as the church's second president until his death in 1877. Utah, meanwhile, is a secular and public university. That's not to say there aren't students or faculty who belong to the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints — head football coach Morgan Scalley and university president Taylor Randall are Mormons, while a 2019 survey conducted by The Daily Utah Chronicle found that about 36% of the student population identified as Latter-day Saints. Still, the numbers pale in comparison to that of its intrastate foe, hence the biblical moniker for the rivalry. It's unclear quite when the feud became sacrosanct. Veteran journalist Dick Harmon recalled first hearing it uttered during radio shows in the 1990s in an op-ed for Deseret News. The "believer vs. pagan" trope doesn't quite reflect the nature of the two schools' relationships to one another. Remember that Brigham Young fellow that BYU gets its title from? He founded the University of Utah. The epithet is a catchy one, nonetheless. It has become a favorite in college football circles over the years, especially as the two sides have been true college football powerhouses in the past two decades. item.description: "I honestly believe that we were the best non-league team ever. Look at that history - it should give the players the confidence that anything is possible." With more than 500 appearances for Altrincham during its golden era of the '70s and '80s, Graham Heathcote knows all about the club's remarkable relationship with the FA Cup, and the giant-killing exploits that forged its identity. One of the club's most legendary figures, he believes they can inspire the current team to pull off another upset against League One Notts County, despite being separated by two divisions. Over the years, Altrincham - currently seventh in the National League - have defeated 17 Football League opponents in the competition, more than any other club that has spent its entire existence in non-league football. During a 14-year playing career at the club, Heathcote secured a crucial part of that history. A 100-goal midfielder in an Altrincham team that despite being part-time, managed to reach the FA Cup's third round in four consecutive seasons between 1978 and 1982. 'We had this determination' "It was an unbelievable achievement because in those days you didn't get weakened sides in the competition like you do now with the bigger clubs," Heathcote told BBC Sport. Now in his 70s, and still living in Altrincham, he added: "During that period, we actually had a better FA Cup record than any side in the old third and fourth divisions." Heathcote was at the heart of some of the club's most memorable achievements, helping the fifth-tier side to defy the odds with third-round draws against first division Everton at Goodison Park in 1975 and a star-studded Spurs at White Hart Lane in 1979. An office worker at Salford docks at the time, Heathcote even scored a penalty in front of the Kop at Anfield against Liverpool in the third round in 1981. It was an era in which Altrincham also won the FA Trophy twice. So what was their secret in cups? "We had this determination, and we became feared at that time," he says. "You reach your level in football, but on a one-off occasion you'd be astonished at where you can raise your game to. You can't do it every week, but it's just a case of getting the mindset right on the day." The club may also have been fuelled by a sense of injustice. item.title: Brennan downs Harlan in regular season finale for District 29-6A title
item.description: Brennan's Jayshawn Mitchell rushes for a first down during the third quarter of a District 29-6A game against Harlan on Friday, November 6, 2026 at Farris Stadium in San Antonio. (Charlie Blalock/For the Express-News) Jayshawn Mitchell whipped his head around as Harlan defenders faded into the background. It was only a matter of time before he found himself in the end zone. The No. 1 junior running back in the nation broke loose for a 93-yard touchdown run that set the tone in Brennan's 30-3 win over Harlan on Friday night at Farris Stadium. "I just tried to keep going," Mitchell said of the long run. "They were pretty close, but I got up out of there and scored." The matchup between Harlan and Brennan determined a district champion for the fourth year in a row. Friday's victory in the regular season fianle gave Brennan the District 29-6A title, the Bears' first district championship since 2024. "We played hard the whole entire game," Mitchell said. "We came out with the dub, and it was just amazing." Brennan head coach Stephen Basore had nothing but praise for the four-star recruit, who received offers to play at LSU and USC earlier this week. "He's just special, and it's not rocket science," the coach said. Brennan moves to 9-1 on the season, while Harlan drops to 8-2 before the playoffs get started next week. Basore said he expects his team to face Laredo LBJ next Thursday at Farris Stadium in the first round of the postseason. Harlan defeated Brennan for last year's district championship, something that the Bears kept at the top of their minds and used as motivation. "They dominated us in physicality and mentality," Brennan junior linebacker Johnas Brewster said of last year's game. "We all got flags. They were taunting us, and we fell for the bait. But this time, we came out, played hard and got our work done." Offensive drives in the first quarter came up empty for both teams until Harlan senior kicker Carlos Cartagena nailed a 38-yard field goal attempt with 3:30 remaining. Harlan's lead was short-lived as Brennan senior kicker Axton Parra hit a 36-yard field goal to tie the game with 10:19 left until halftime. But Brennan really started gaining momentum when junior defensive back Josiah Tolefree recovered a Harlan fumble to get the Bears' offense back on the field. Mitchell's 93-yard touchdown run came on the very next play. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images Cubs’ Pete Crow-Armstrong wins NL Platinum Glove Award appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Pete Crow-Armstrong and the Chicago Cubs have more hardware to celebrate. Just days after helping Chicago win the National League Team Gold Glove , the Cubs’ center fielder was named the 2026 NL Platinum Glove Award winner. Rawlings announced the honor on Friday, with New York Yankees outfielder Cody Bellinger taking home the American League Platinum Glove . The award recognizes the best overall defensive player in each league, chosen from the pool of Gold Glove winners. Crow-Armstrong earned his place in that group by winning his second straight Gold Glove in center field. It was hardly a close call at the position. He led the league with 26 Outs Above Average and 10 Defensive Runs Saved, cementing his status as one of the most dynamic defenders in baseball. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) What made his 2026 season even more special was what he did at the plate. Crow-Armstrong hit .280 with 45 home runs, 107 RBIs and 41 stolen bases, joining the exclusive 40/40 club . It was another big step forward for the 24-year-old, who has quickly developed into one of the brightest young stars in all of baseball. He was far from the only Cub who shined with the glove. Alex Bregman won his first Gold Glove as a member of the Cubs at third base, becoming the first Chicago third baseman to win the award since Ron Santo. Ian Happ, Dansby Swanson and Seiya Suzuki were also named finalists, giving the Cubs five Gold Glove finalists, tied with the Toronto Blue Jays for the most in the majors. As a team, the Cubs led the league with 115 Outs Above Average and 73 Defensive Runs Saved, earning their second straight NL Team Gold Glove. The Blue Jays took home the AL honor. Despite the elite defense, Chicago’s season ended earlier than hoped. The Cubs finished 89-73 and were eliminated by the San Diego Padres in the NL Wild Card Series . Still, the future looks bright on the North Side with Crow-Armstrong leading the way . With his rare combination of power, speed and elite defense, he has established himself as one of the most complete players in baseball, and the Cubs will be counting on him to lead a deeper postseason push in 2027. item.description: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Head coach Mike Macdonald of the Seattle Seahawks looks on from the sidelines during the game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Wevers/Getty Images) Getty The Seattle Seahawks have been seen as a potential landing spot for Jonathan Taylor, but one NFL insider believes there is only one serious suitor for the All-Pro running back — and it’s not Seattle. The Seahawks struggled on the ground for much of the season, stung by the departure of Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III in free agency and injuries to their top two backs. Though they have gotten some relief with the returns of Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price, some NFL insiders believed they could still take a home-run swing at Taylor on the trade market. A new report from SI.com NFL insider Albert Breer revealed that they may be out of the running entirely. Seahawks Not Pursuing Jonathan Taylor In an update in the days before the NFL trade deadline, Breer reported that the Colts are holding out for a big trade offer for their star running back. “So how much will it cost? My understanding is a first-round pick, or the equivalent in a Christian McCaffrey–level package (the 49ers sent 2023 second-, third- and fourth-round picks, and a 2024 fifth-rounder to the Panthers for McCaffrey in October 2023) would likely get it done, and the Colts haven’t gotten that price,” Breer reported. Not many teams are willing to pay that price. Breer reported that there have been three teams in touch with the Colts about Taylor, with just one a “serious” contender. The Seahawks are not on either list. “The Giants, Broncos and Vikings have inquired, and discussed it, and it appears Denver and Minnesota might be a little less inclined to trade for Taylor now,” Breer wrote. “Conversely, the indication I’ve gotten is that while the Giants aren’t offering what Indy wants, they are a serious suitor.” Seahawks Struggled With Top Running Backs Returning The Seahawks had been looking forward to the returns of Charbonnet and Price, but the offense failed to click with both on the field in last week’s loss to the Chicago Bears . Charbonnet didn’t perform any better against an aggressive Bears defense, rushing for 23 yards on six carries. The Seahawks did make a move in their backfield, announcing on Friday that they released running back Velus Jones Jr., who had just nine carries for 28 yards and one reception for minus-1 yard in six games this season. item.description: Ilia Topuria Alexander Volkanovski Getty Former UFC featherweight champion and lightweight champion Ilia Topuria explained why he won’t rematch Alexander Volkanovski. Topuria knocked out Volkanovski to win the UFC featherweight title back at UFC 298 in February 2024. But while he already beat him once, the Georgian says he has no interest in fighting Volkanovski again. Here’s why. Ilia Topuria Explains Why He Won’t Rematch Alexander Volkanovski Speaking to ABC, Topuria explained why he won’t fight Volkanovski for a second time. “I have so much affection and respect for him that I couldn’t hit him. I like him too much. There are already things I don’t want to do. What for? It would be a very competitive fight, even though I beat him once. For me, he’s the best featherweight that has ever existed, the most dominant. I was the champion, and I’ve done things that nobody else has done, but I left the division. He’s done much more at that weight than I have. It’s been many years,” Topuria said (via Bloody Elbow ). Ilia Topuria Gunning for Paddy Pimblett While a fight against Volkanovski is clearly off the table, a matchup against Paddy Pimblett is what Topuria wants right now, and it’s a fight that makes a whole ton of sense given where both men currently sit in the UFC lightweight division. It seems like UFC lightweight champion Justin Gaethje will fight either Volkanovski or Arman Tsarukyan in his first title defense or retire if he wants to. That leaves Topuria and Pimblett open and available to fight each other, and it’s a fight that all MMA fans want, as it would put two of the best lightweights in the world against one another with a likely title shot at 155 lbs on the line. We’ll have to wait and see what the UFC ends up doing with all of these top lightweights, but one thing is for sure, and that’s that Topuria has no interest in fighting Volkanovski again, as he respects him far too much and doesn’t want to step into the Octagon and hurt him again, even though he’s already done it once before. Kuminga connected with his point guard twice on the left wing for catch-and-shoot threes on the move. Their playstyles complement each other seamlessly, as the 6-foot-7 forward's downhill athleticism creates defensive gaps for Ball to exploit off the catch. Minnesota will miss its star Anthony Edwards for up to two months after successful arthroscopic surgery on his right knee. The 27-year-old has averaged 1.9 steals this season, including a season-high three against the Rockets and the San Antonio Spurs last Saturday. Finch praised him for staying out of foul trouble in the past few games. Ball finished with four fouls in the last two games and averages 4.2 fouls per game, a career-high.
